data.title: From 4 Million Illegal Transactions To 40 Years In Prison, Empire Market Co-Creator To Surrender $101 Million In Bitcoin
data.description:
The operator of one of the dark web’s largest drug marketplaces will surrender more than $100 million in cryptocurrency after receiving a 40-year prison sentence for helping run a platform that facilitated over four million illegal transactions.

Raheim Hamilton, 30, agreed to forfeit 1,230 bitcoin worth approximately $101 million, 24.4 ether valued at around $60,000, and three properties in Virginia.

US District Judge Steven C. Seeger also imposed a $5 million fine following Hamilton’s sentencing in Chicago on 5 October.

Dark Web Drug Market Boss Faces Prison And a Massive Bitcoin Forfeiture

Raheim Hamilton, co-founder of darknet marketplace Empire Market, received a 40-year federal prison sentence.

Hamilton pleaded guilty to a federal drug conspiracy charge. He agreed to forfeit about 1,230… pic.twitter.com/HxzGMGO9lT

— BSCN (@BSCNews) October 9, 2026

Empire Market Facilitated More Than $430 Million In Transactions

Hamilton co-created and operated Empire Market with Thomas Pavey between 2018 and 2020.

The platform became a major online marketplace for illegal goods, allowing users to buy and sell drugs, stolen account credentials, personal information, counterfeit currency and computer hacking tools.

Prosecutors said the marketplace facilitated more than four million transactions worth over $430 million during its operation.

Drug sales accounted for nearly $375 million of the total, making narcotics the platform’s largest source of business.

The drugs sold included fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine and heroin.

According to the US Department of Justice (DOJ), the marketplace handled approximately 13.3 kilograms of fentanyl, 446.7 kilograms of cocaine, 72 kilograms of methamphetamine and 103.4 kilograms of heroin.

Empire Market operated as a hidden service on the dark web, accessible through the Tor browser.

At its peak in August 2020, it had approximately 1.68 million registered users, more than 5,000 vendors and nearly 360,000 buyers.

🚨 🇺🇸 Empire Market co-creator sentenced to 40 years for operating $430 million dark web marketplace

Raheim Hamilton, 30, also known online as “Sydney” and “ZeroAngel,” has been sentenced to 40 years in federal prison and fined $5 million.

Hamilton and co-creator Thomas Pavey… pic.twitter.com/5B3bT8sdRa

— Dark Web Informer (@DarkWebInformer) October 8, 2026

How Did Empire Market Help Users Conceal Illegal Transactions?

Cryptocurrency was mandatory for transactions on Empire Market, while Hamilton and Pavey encouraged users to employ mixing services to make the movement of funds harder to trace.

The DOJ said the pair also encouraged encrypted communications and allowed buyers to rate vendors based on how effectively they concealed drugs in packages sent to customers.

These measures were intended to make illegal activities harder for law enforcement to detect.

The platform also employed moderators to settle disputes between buyers and sellers, with Hamilton supervising around five moderators and handling some disputes himself.

Investigators carried out undercover purchases between April 2019 and May 2020, acquiring methamphetamine and heroin through the marketplace.

Authorities also intercepted a package containing 443.5 grams of methamphetamine ordered through the site.

The DOJ announced charges against Hamilton and Pavey in 2024 and said investigators had seized approximately $75 million in cryptocurrency during the investigation.

Hamilton And Pavey Face Heavy Financial Penalties

Hamilton pleaded guilty to a federal drug conspiracy charge in January 2026, admitting his role in operating the marketplace.

His sentence combines a lengthy prison term with the forfeiture of cryptocurrency and property, alongside the $5 million fine.

His co-conspirator, Pavey, 41, of Ormond Beach, Florida, pleaded guilty last year and admitted to helping create and operate Empire Market.

Pavey agreed to forfeit approximately 1,584 bitcoin, two boxes containing 25-ounce gold bars, three cars and two properties in Florida.

His sentencing is scheduled for later in October.

The financial penalties follow the marketplace’s collapse in 2020.

Empire Market disappeared abruptly, with reports alleging that its operators took approximately $30 million in bitcoin belonging to users.

US Authorities Continue Targeting Dark Web Crime

The Empire Market case is part of a wider effort by US authorities to disrupt online marketplaces and financial services used for criminal activity.

In February 2026, the US government seized approximately $400 million in cryptocurrency, real estate and cash linked to Helix, a bitcoin mixing service that the DOJ said had been used to launder money for drug traffickers and other criminals.

Recently the U.S. government gained legal title over more than $400 million in seized assets, including cryptocurrency and real estate, forfeited from Larry Dean Harmon who operated darknet mixing service Helix.

Learn more about this investigation here: https://t.co/f2qiEPCNRHpic.twitter.com/UFcFRLRC8A

— FBI Cyber Division (@FBICyberDiv) January 30, 2026

The agency has also pursued operators of other dark web marketplaces.

In February 2026, Ruis-Sian Lin, the alleged operator of Incognito Market, received a 30-year federal prison sentence.

These cases demonstrate the financial and criminal penalties facing operators of platforms that facilitate illegal transactions, even when cryptocurrency and encryption are used to conceal activity.

data.title: GTA VI Leaker Returns With More Spoilers as $CYBERLEEK Crypto Rebounds 200%
data.description:
Pseudonymous Grand Theft Auto VI leaker “Cyberleek” has returned from an online hiatus with 25 minutes of alleged gameplay footage, including provocative character scenes and a reported first-person mode, while continuing to promote their cryptocurrency token, $CYBERLEEK.

GTA 6 LEAK V30 #cyberleek #gta #gtavi #gta6 #gtavıleak #leakedvideo 👋 https://t.co/RNNX1eBf4S

— CyberLeek (@cyb3rleek_ar_io) October 9, 2026

The latest leak has renewed concerns among gamers that major details of Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated title could emerge before its November release. It has also brought fresh attention to Cyberleek’s crypto promotion, with the token’s market capitalization reportedly jumping 200% over the past two days despite remaining far below its earlier peak.

Cyberleek returned this week claiming to have released previously unseen open-world gameplay and mission cutscenes from GTA VI. Among the footage described in the report are scenes showing protagonist Jason running around naked and his in-game partner Lucia wearing only bikini bottoms. The clips also reportedly reveal a first-person mode, although the claims have not been independently verified in the supplied report.

The leaker first published a batch of GTA VI footage on August 18, using the attention to promote $CYBERLEEK. Cyberleek also framed the leaks as a consumer-rights protest against the decision to drop physical game discs, presenting the activity as more than a bid to capitalize on anticipation surrounding the game.

Another leg? $CYBERLEEK https://t.co/hl9zslLkoF

— Tega 🚫 (@tega_exe) October 8, 2026

The renewed activity could make it harder for players to avoid spoilers as the release date approaches. Some social media users have already suggested muting specific keywords to reduce the chances of encountering leaked story details or gameplay clips before they can experience the game themselves.

$CYBERLEEK Jumps 200% but Remains 94% Below Its Peak

The latest leaks have coincided with a short-term rebound in $CYBERLEEK’s market capitalization. According to the report, the token recorded two modest jumps over the past two days, bringing its market cap up by approximately 200%.

That recovery, however, has done little to reverse the token’s broader decline. $CYBERLEEK remains down about 94% from its late-August peak of nearly $40 million, which followed Cyberleek’s initial release of GTA VI leaks.

靠 $CYBERLEEK 赚了 +1,693.7 SOL 没错，我现在几天赚到的钱，过去可能一辈子都赚不到 最近靠 memecoin 赚钱简单得有点离谱 没什么秘密，每天打开电脑，扫几只币，然后挑出最有可能把钱塞进我口袋的那一只 如果你现在还赚不到钱，要么你太菜，要么就是跟错了人 下一只已经在找了 https://t.co/Zo61czNZqJ

— DuDu (@dudunode) August 25, 2026

The price movements highlight the speculative nature of tokens promoted around viral internet events. In this case, attention generated by a major gaming franchise has served as a promotional hook for a crypto asset whose market value has fluctuated sharply. The timing of the latest rebound does not, by itself, establish that the new footage caused the increase or that the token’s promotion involved market manipulation.

Cyberleek’s activity nevertheless illustrates how unreleased games and online speculation can become intertwined with cryptocurrency promotion, turning leaks into a potential source of attention for a token long after its initial hype has faded.

Rockstar and Take-Two Pursue the Leaker as Launch Nears

The earlier leaks prompted Rockstar Games to publicly express its frustration ahead of a 20-minute streaming event partnered with Netflix. The developer said its team was “heartbroken” and warned that the intended game experience could be affected by spoilers circulating before launch.

Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, has also reportedly filed multiple subpoenas targeting platforms including Discord, Microsoft and X in an effort to identify the person behind the leaks.

See the next evolution in the groundbreaking Grand Theft Auto series. Watch Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look. Now on Netflix: https://t.co/rGvIlqDzbx https://t.co/vMhoBbNrZD

— Netflix India (@NetflixIndia) August 27, 2026

The stakes are significant for a title that has attracted enormous anticipation. GTA VI is scheduled to launch on November 19 and has reportedly already generated nearly $430 million in pre-orders. Further leaks could undermine the carefully managed rollout of one of the gaming's most anticipated releases, while also giving Cyberleek additional opportunities to draw attention to $Cyberleek.

With the launch approaching, the leaker’s return puts two different forms of speculation back in the spotlight: gamers’ fears of having major story moments spoiled, and traders’ hopes that renewed viral attention might revive a token that has lost most of its earlier market value.

data.title: Ethereum And Bitcoin Developers Turn To Anthropic’s AI Scanner As Concerns Grow Over Faster Cyberattacks
data.description:
Crypto Developers Queue Up For Anthropic's Free AI Security Scans

Two of the best-known names in blockchain software have asked Anthropic to comb through their code for weaknesses.

Nethermind, an Ethereum client developer, and ZEUS, a Bitcoin and Lightning wallet, were among several crypto companies that applied on 9 October 2026 to OSS Scanner, a service Anthropic launched a day earlier.

The programme gives open-source projects vulnerability reports produced by the company's most capable AI models, with the aim of letting developers fix flaws before attackers find them.

🛡️ Nethermind and ZEUS are among crypto projects applying for Anthropic's new OSS Scanner: security reports from its strongest models (incl. Claude Mythos) for open-source code.

Goal: fix bugs before attackers find them.#AI#Crypto
🟢 Signal: Positive

— Meeload.Crypto 🇮🇷 (@Meeload001) October 9, 2026

What Is OSS Scanner And How Does It Work?

OSS Scanner is an opt-in service that grows out of Anthropic's earlier Project Glasswing.

Under that work, the company already scanned open-source software regularly and sent reports only after human review.

That checking step proved to be the bottleneck, and Anthropic admitted that it was "not always able to share vulnerabilities as quickly as we would like."

To secure open-source software, we’re launching OSS Scanner.

We’ll use our frontier models to periodically scan opted-in open-source projects for vulnerabilities, at no cost. Our reports will provide a proof-of-concept, explanation, and suggested fix.https://t.co/UFFrLUd25U

— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) October 8, 2026

The new service removes the wait.

Reports go to participating projects as soon as their code has been scanned.

Anthropic said in its announcement,

"These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos) to give open-source projects the largest defensive advantage."

Each report includes a reproducible example of the weakness, an explanation of the affected code and, where available, a suggested patch.

Who Has Applied So Far?

Requests appear as pull requests in the OSS Scanner GitHub repository.

Nethermind asked for its entire repository to be audited in request number 38.

ZEUS, which lets users hold their own Bitcoin, asked for checks on areas that touch payments, private keys and links to Lightning services, in request number 47.

VirtEngine, a decentralised cloud computing marketplace built as a Cosmos SDK chain, filed request number 46.

The list extends well beyond crypto.

Developers of AI assistants, agent-security tools and machine-learning infrastructure have also applied, along with teams behind software development tools, cloud storage and energy-system controls.

These remain requests only.

None of the applicants has yet been confirmed, and Anthropic has not given a timetable for approvals or first reports.

How Will Anthropic Choose Which Projects Get In?

Each application will be judged individually.

Anthropic said it will look at how important a project is to infrastructure and user security, how exposed it is to remote attacks, and how many users or other projects depend on it.

It will also consider whether a team can realistically review and act on the findings it receives.

Why Did Anthropic Skip Human Review?

The answer lies in the numbers.

Over six months, Anthropic's models flagged more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities in widely used open-source projects.

Researchers had manually checked only about 6,000 of them, leaving a large backlog.

The trade-off is accuracy.

Anthropic just opened OSS Scanner. Free AI vulnerability scans for open-source projects that opt in. Same stack they used on Project Glasswing.

Their own numbers: 29,000+ candidate vulns in 6 months. Only about 6,000 got human review. So raw model reports are the product now.…

— Santhosh Patel (@santhosh_patell) October 9, 2026

Because reports now arrive unverified, Anthropic accepts that some may carry wrong severity ratings or describe flaws that do not apply to a project's security design.

In early testing, outside penetration testers examined 97 high-severity and critical findings across 48 projects.

A total of 85, or roughly 88 per cent, met the company's standard for coordinated disclosure.

Of the remaining 12, eleven were genuine problems that duplicated existing reports, and one was invalid.

Maintainers must check each finding themselves before deciding what to change, and Anthropic will keep its human-reviewed process for projects that cannot cope with large volumes of automated reports.

Why Are Crypto Teams So Keen To Join?

Crypto software holds money directly, which makes a single flaw costly.

Several firms have already reported attacks this year that they believe were helped by AI.

Bitcoin swap provider Boltz halted its services on 3 August 2026, saying attackers were building exploits faster than its team could patch them.

Its self-custodial design kept customer funds safe, but the shutdown disrupted services that relied on it, including ZEUS, which temporarily disabled swaps.

UPDATE ON THE FUTURE OF BOLTZ 📢

Over the past couple of months, AI-assisted attackers have been targeting Boltz with increasing frequency, intensity and sophistication. Several of these attacks succeeded, but because Boltz is non-custodial, user funds were never at risk. The…

— Boltz - Non-Custodial Bitcoin Bridge (@Boltzhq) August 12, 2026

Crypto-payment service PayPerQ also reported repeated attacks it suspected were AI-powered.

Other security efforts point the same way.

Bitcoin Red Team reported 4,962 potential vulnerabilities across 390 Bitcoin-related projects after about 30 hours of AI-assisted code review in August, with 720 rated high or critical, though each needed verification.

Bitcoin Red Team update: we've grown to 16 globally distributed people working 24/7

We're running a large-scale ecosystem security audit across bitcoin code bases.

27.5 hours in, we've filed 4,962 findings across 390 projects. 85 critical and 635 high severity issues.

We're at… pic.twitter.com/iRCylprbY1

— calle (@callebtc) August 5, 2026

Kraken's parent company, Payward, also joined the Claude Mythos security programme in August to examine its own systems.

Could AI Tip The Balance Towards Attackers?

Anthropic itself has cautioned that AI may favour attackers in the near term, because exploiting flaws is becoming cheaper while verifying and fixing them still depends on people.

Security experts have raised a related worry that defenders could fall behind if access to powerful models is uneven.

OSS Scanner is part of the Anthropic Cyber Mission, announced on 8 October 2026.

Alongside it, the company introduced the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which offers AI models, engineering support and threat research to organisations protecting power grids, transport networks and industrial systems.

Partners include CrowdStrike, Accenture, Deloitte and Palo Alto Networks.

Anthropic just put Claude on the power grid's side.

New Critical Infrastructure Defense Program: frontier models + on-site engineers for firms securing power, water, and transport. 11 partners including CrowdStrike, Dragos, and Rockwell. Free OSS Scanner too.

Can AI keep the… pic.twitter.com/5TjriLL8Ja

— Innoworkspro (@innoworkspro) October 9, 2026

Maintainers who want a place in OSS Scanner can apply through its GitHub repository using the published enrolment template, and approved projects will receive regular scans at no cost.

data.title: Google Is Giving AI Agents Their Own Email Addresses To Work Like Real Employees And Handle Office Tasks
data.description:
Google Cloud is introducing an AI agent designed to take over entire workplace tasks, from gathering information across business applications to producing finished documents and running code.

Rather than requiring employees to guide AI through every step, the system allows them to set an objective and leave the agent to work towards the result.

Announced by Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian at the Gemini at Work 2026 event on 8 October 2026, the Gemini Agent can operate across Google's workplace tools and third-party services, with tasks continuing in the cloud even after users close their laptops.

Kurian described the changing approach to work by saying, "work now starts in the prompt window."

Tune in now for #GeminiAtWork. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian takes the stage to showcase how our customers around the world are transforming their organizations using Gemini. https://t.co/nk5TsqPw5i

— Google Cloud (@googlecloud) October 8, 2026

Gemini Agent Can Handle Work Across Google, Microsoft And Slack

The Gemini Agent connects Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Chat and Calendar, while also supporting Microsoft 365 and Slack.

It can retrieve information from different applications, organise relevant material and complete tasks without requiring employees to manage every stage manually.

2️⃣ Gemini connects to the apps you already run like Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira, Confluence, Git, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and any MCP server.

Every tool call passes through our Agent Gateway to enforce policy and block data leaks. pic.twitter.com/UP9VyR2ofn

— Google Cloud Tech (@GoogleCloudTech) October 8, 2026

For example, an employee preparing for a meeting could ask the agent to gather information from email conversations, locate supporting documents, check spreadsheet figures and prepare a briefing.

The system is designed to carry out these connected steps and return the completed work, rather than simply providing instructions on how to do it.

Today, we are announcing our new Gemini agent for your business—a universal cloud agent running 24/7 to get your work done.

It arrives knowing your tools, data, and work history; it works across knowledge work, content, and code; and it comes with built-in governance to help… pic.twitter.com/MQ2NDSJG2n

— Google Cloud (@googlecloud) October 8, 2026

Its cloud-based operation also allows tasks to continue for hours or days, even when the user is no longer actively working on them.

The agent can connect to business platforms such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Jira, Snowflake and BigQuery, as well as other systems that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that allows AI tools to connect with software and external data sources.

Google is also allowing the agent to use AI models beyond its own Gemini family.

The system can coordinate work across Gemini and Anthropic's Claude models, selecting what Google considers the most suitable option for each task based on quality and cost.

The company plans to add support for more models over time.

#6: Gemini is not tied to one model.

Gemini is the agent. The model underneath is a separate choice, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬: our model, a third-party model, or an open model—whichever model fits the job. pic.twitter.com/SYHzKj0Icd

— Google Cloud (@googlecloud) October 8, 2026

Companies Can Give AI Agents Their Own Work Identities

Beyond completing individual assignments, the Gemini Agent introduces what Google calls "coworker agents", which businesses can create to take on defined responsibilities.

A manager could, for instance, establish an AI agent to act as an events coordinator.

The agent would receive its own Google Workspace account, including an email address, calendar and Drive storage, and appear in the company's directory.

This setup allows businesses to assign work to AI agents in a way that resembles collaboration with human colleagues.

Each agent can access information made available to it, with permissions and administrative controls intended to limit its access to company resources.

#3: Gemini is one agent, that works everywhere. It can dynamically create a roster of sub-agents—temporary, job-specific agents, each with their own identity—to tackle multi-step tasks.

In addition, Gemini can act as a coworker agent—more like a team member, with a persistent,… pic.twitter.com/OFlLtyaz7O

— Google Cloud (@googlecloud) October 8, 2026

The approach places Google in a growing market for AI systems that can operate across applications and pursue goals with less direct supervision.

OpenAI introduced its always-on agents, known as dots, in September 2026, while other AI platforms have also explored agents with their own identities and responsibilities.

How Will Google Keep Autonomous AI Agents Under Control?

Giving AI systems the ability to act across workplace applications creates security risks, particularly when agents can access emails, documents and internal business systems.

Google's approach is to treat each agent like an employee with a verifiable identity.

Every agent receives a cryptographically attested identity, while its actions are recorded in an audit trail that attributes activity to the agent responsible.

The company has also introduced an Agent Sandbox, an isolated environment intended to prevent agents from interfering with other parts of a system.

Their network traffic passes through Agent Gateway, which Google describes as an "AI network firewall".

However, keeping AI agents contained remains a challenge for the industry.

In July 2026, researchers at Accomplish AI reported that the local mode of Anthropic's Claude Cowork could escape its Linux virtual machine on Macs and access files on the host computer.

The incident illustrates why businesses need safeguards beyond an agent's ability to complete tasks successfully.

Google Adds Spending Limits As AI Agent Costs Grow

The cost of running autonomous agents is another concern for businesses, as these systems can consume large amounts of tokens, the units of text that AI models process and generate.

Google said nearly 500 of its customers processed more than one trillion tokens each over the past year.

In the last year, nearly 500 Cloud customers have each processed more than one trillion tokens.

At that volume, you are not experimenting; you are running the business on it.

It’s happening every second of the day, somewhere around the world. pic.twitter.com/OcHgZsdAQp

— Google Cloud (@googlecloud) October 8, 2026

To help businesses control spending, the Gemini Agent includes real-time expenditure limits.

When a project reaches its configured cap, the agent pauses until an authorised user approves its resumption.

These controls sit alongside the platform's security, administration and governance features, which are designed to help companies manage how agents use their resources and perform work.

When Can Businesses Start Using The Gemini Agent?

Google has not announced pricing or a general availability date for the Gemini Agent.

Versions designed for financial services and legal work are currently in preview, while offerings for government, healthcare and retail are listed as coming soon.

The initial focus is on enterprise customers, with no confirmed timeline for a wider consumer release.

The launch expands Google's efforts to integrate AI into everyday business operations, moving beyond tools that answer questions or generate content towards systems that can plan and execute multi-step tasks.

Adoption will depend not only on how much work these agents can complete independently, but also on whether businesses can manage their access, security risks and operating costs.

data.title: Justin Sun’s AI Math Prize Names Winners — But Where’s the $1 Million?
data.description:
Three mathematicians have reportedly solved six long-standing mathematical problems using AI-assisted methods, but the Justin Sun Prize’s headline $1 million reward comes with a significant caveat: the top payout is reserved for just seven designated problems, while the compensation for other solvers remains unclear.

孫哥說：「我的財富建立在數學之上」，整個區塊鏈產業，都奠基於少數幾個密碼學基本與數學假設，因此決定設立 Justin Sun Prize，回饋根基。 🌟 巔峰級數學難題只要能證明，每題就提供 100 萬美元（不分人類或是 AI） #JustinSunPrize https://t.co/SEIiDC6rrU

— 動區動趨 BlockTempo (@BlockTempo) September 17, 2026

Justin Sun has spent the past week announcing winners of the prize, an initiative launched to reward mathematicians who use artificial intelligence to tackle difficult mathematical questions. Yet as the winners are named, questions remain over how much they are entitled to receive, who decides the payouts and when the promised stablecoins will be distributed.

The $1 Million Promise Has a Major Catch

According to the prize’s official website, three individuals have solved six problems so far. In an October 5 announcement, the Office of Justin Sun named independent researcher Wouter van Doorn, mathematics Ph.D. student Quanyu Tang and Yanyang Li, a mathematics researcher at Southeast University in Nanjing, as recipients for their work on problems associated with the late Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős.

The first winners of the Justin Sun Prize have been confirmed. Congratulations to Wouter van Doorn, Yanyang Li, and Quanyu Tang on their solutions to problems from the Erdős catalogue. More details on the winners and their work coming soon. QUOD PROBATUR, SOLVITUR. https://t.co/xeJFkEhQMu

— The Justin Sun Prize (@JustinSunPrize) October 3, 2026

The problems include Erdős Problem #650, which concerns how many integers can always be matched to distinct multiples within a given interval. Van Doorn also produced computer-checkable proofs in Lean, a software system used to formally verify mathematical reasoning.

The prize presents the work as an example of AI-assisted mathematical discovery combined with formal verification, which can help make proofs independently checkable. But recognition for solving a problem does not necessarily mean a researcher will receive the headline reward advertised when the initiative was launched.

That distinction sits at the heart of the questions now surrounding the prize.

The Justin Sun Prize was promoted as an award equivalent to $1 million in stablecoins. Its rules, however, limit the million-dollar USDT or USDC payouts to solvers of problems designated as “pinnacle problems.”

There are only seven such problems among the more than 1,000 listed on the prize website. That leaves a much larger pool of mathematical challenges for which the financial reward is less clearly defined.

The website describes five categories of problems, but it does not specify exactly how much researchers who solve problems outside the pinnacle category can expect to receive. Instead, it says that “the specific capital allocation” for other prizes will be determined by an Academic Committee.

The committee’s membership and the criteria it will use to set compensation have not been clearly disclosed in the supplied material. As a result, researchers may be able to determine which problems qualify for recognition without being able to establish in advance what solving them will pay.

The prize says recipients can choose to receive their awards in USDT on TRON using the TRC-20 standard or USDC on Ethereum using ERC-20. But specifying the payment networks does not answer the more basic questions of how much each winner is owed or when the funds will arrive.

Funding Questions Persist as Winners Are Announced

The uncertainty over payouts follows an earlier report by Protos, which questioned whether the prize had demonstrated that funds were available to cover its advertised stablecoin rewards. Protos noted at launch that Sun had announced the award without publicly providing proof of funds backing the promised payouts.

以前不懂王兴为什么天天在饭否发帖，一个社交网站只有老板一个用户。 后来觉得，整个世界只有一个用户，挺浪漫的。 直到我有了 @Poloniex 。 全球唯一一家只有老板自己在用的交易所。 孤独到极致，也是一种自由。

— H.E. Justin Sun 👨‍🚀 🌞 (@justinsuntron) October 5, 2026

The latest winners’ announcement has not, according to the material provided, been accompanied by public documentation showing how the prize money is held or whether it has been placed in escrow. That absence does not establish that the prize lacks the money to pay winners, but it leaves the funding arrangements difficult for outsiders to assess.

Sun, the founder of TRON, has positioned the initiative as a way to support mathematical research, formal verification and AI-assisted scientific discovery. The prize’s earlier announcements also highlighted solutions and formalized proofs across a broader set of mathematical problems, including work on the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations.

The precise relationship between those earlier awards and the newly announced Erdős-problem recipients should be distinguished when assessing the total number of winners and the amounts awarded.

At #TOKEN2049, @justinsuntron discussed TRON’s focus on real-world use, infrastructure for AI agents and the vision behind the @JustinSunPrize. Read the main-stage conversation recap. 👇 https://t.co/wrSg9bgmPl

— TRON DAO (@trondao) October 9, 2026

For now, the latest announcements demonstrate that researchers are being recognized for their work. They do not, on their own, establish how much each recipient will receive or when payment will be made.

Until the prize clarifies its payout criteria, identifies the body responsible for allocating rewards and provides greater transparency around funding, its headline $1 million figure will remain only part of the story.

data.title: Standard Chartered Targets Late 2026 To Launch Regulated Crypto and Tokenised Asset Custody Services in Singapore
data.description:
Standard Chartered Prepares Institutional Digital Asset Safekeeping Service in Singapore

Standard Chartered Bank (Singapore) Limited aims to introduce safekeeping services for selected cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and tokenised real-world assets by the end of the year.

The institutional service caters exclusively to corporate clients qualifying as accredited investors and remains subject to local regulatory approvals.

By housing digital custody within its Financing and Securities Services division, the bank intends to create an operational bridge where institutional clients can seamlessly transition between conventional securities and tokenised financial products.

JUST IN: Standard Chartered plans to launch crypto custody services for institutional clients in Singapore.

The move would add another major bank to the regulated infrastructure supporting digital assets. pic.twitter.com/ItP1VWL5Qm

— CryptosRus (@CryptosR_Us) October 8, 2026

How Will Traditional and Tokenised Assets Integration Work?

The planned setup integrates conventional asset servicing, tokenisation, and custody across the complete investment lifecycle.

Under this unified framework, institutional investors can convert standard holdings into tokenised formats while keeping all assets under one bank-grade umbrella.

The bank has not disclosed which specific tokens or stablecoin issuers will receive support at launch.

Growing appetite among institutional funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and precious metal vehicles underpins the timing of the rollout.

Ying Ying Tan, global head for digital assets and securities services at Standard Chartered, noted,

"Institutions are showing growing interest in tokenized funds, ETFs, and precious metals. They want more efficient ways of holding, transferring, and mobilizing those assets."

Singapore Chief Executive Officer Patrick Lee explained that the city-state offers an ideal environment for institutional adoption.

Lee said,

"Singapore is an important centre for financial innovation, with a strong institutional ecosystem and growing demand for trusted digital asset solutions. Robust infrastructure will be critical to supporting the secure movement, safekeeping, and servicing of tokenised assets at an institutional scale."

Where Does Singapore Fit into the Global Safeguarding Network?

Singapore represents the latest addition to Standard Chartered’s international digital asset safekeeping footprint, joining established operations in the United Arab Emirates, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong.

Ole Matthiessen, global head of transaction services and digital assets, highlighted that institutional clients demand the safety of a global systemically important bank.

Matthiessen stated,

"Secure and regulated custody is a critical foundation of the digital asset ecosystem.”

He added that the bank will continue investing in digital asset capabilities across major financial hubs as institutional demand increases.

The Singapore expansion builds upon internal restructuring efforts regarding the bank's crypto operations.

Standard Chartered previously established Zodia Custody in 2020 alongside Northern Trust, securing additional investment from institutions including SBI Holdings, Emirates NBD, and National Australia Bank.

In May 2026, stakeholders accepted a non-binding offer allowing Standard Chartered to acquire Zodia Custody’s core business, integrating regulated custody directly into its Financing and Securities Services division while redirecting Zodia Solutions under SC Ventures to supply digital infrastructure.

Zodia Custody integrated onto Metaco's network, the custody platform Ripple acquired, and Standard Chartered later moved to acquire Zodia's custody business outright. A bank buying a custody arm built on Ripple's infrastructure is worth watching. pic.twitter.com/xHvAD34iDC

— Jake Claver, QFOP (@beyond_broke) September 27, 2026

Zodia has operated in Singapore since September 2023 and acquired a payment institution licence in Luxembourg in June 2026 to support regulated stablecoin operations across the European Union.

How Extensive Is the Existing Banking Footprint Across Crypto Markets?

Standard Chartered has built out operational channels across multiple international centers and crypto platforms:

  • Trading Operations: The bank’s UK entity began handling deliverable spot bitcoin and ether trades for institutional clients in July 2025, while its Dubai branch launched equivalent trading through its foreign-exchange platform in September 2026.

BREAKING:

Standard Chartered just became the first global systemically important bank to offer this in the Gulf.

Institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot trading. Live in the UAE.

Through Standard Chartered DIFC. Regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority.
Integrated… pic.twitter.com/WkMnywmdlv

— Crypto Tice (@CryptoTice_) September 5, 2026

  • Exchange Integration: In June 2026, the bank struck a commercial agreement with exchange CoinMENA to manage fiat on-ramps, off-ramps, client money accounts, and virtual account transaction services.

🤝 Major milestone for MENA digital assets!

CoinMENA (@CoinMENA) has signed a banking agreement with Standard Chartered (@StanChart) to enhance fiat on/off-ramps with faster funding, efficient payouts, and real-time payment rails. 🌐#CoinMENA#StandardChartered#MENA#FinTechpic.twitter.com/rGRP8gEZT9

— CoinMENA | كوين مينا (@CoinMENA) June 17, 2026

  • Fiat Settlement: Standard Chartered facilitates real-time movement of Singapore dollars ($1 SGD is approximately $0.78) for Coinbase customers in Singapore. The arrangement spans trading, custody, staking, and lending, allowing corporate users to settle digital asset trades with any custodian of their choice.

  • Hong Kong & Global Alliances: In May 2026, the bank agreed to provide crypto safekeeping for SOLOWIN Holdings in Hong Kong, followed by an expanded September partnership with LMAX Group linking custody infrastructure to institutional trading desks in Luxembourg and Dubai.

We're pleased to share that we have appointed @StanChart as our digital asset custodian, through Standard Chartered's DIFC branch in Dubai and Standard Chartered Luxembourg S.A.

LMAX Group is the first client to join Standard Chartered Luxembourg's digital asset custody… pic.twitter.com/ml1KThbqSG

— LMAX Group (@LMAX) September 16, 2026

What Regulatory Landscape Shapes Singapore Market Access?

The proposed custody service operates within local rules governed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under the Payment Services Act.

Regulatory oversight of stablecoins continues to take shape; on 1 September 2026, MAS released regulatory proposals targeting single-currency stablecoin issuers, focusing on reserve backing, redemption rights, and criteria for recognizing qualified foreign stablecoins.

🇸🇬 JUST IN: Singapore proposes BANNING stablecoin issuers from paying yield to holders.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore wants 100% reserve backing at all times, segregated custody, stress testing, and mandatory wind-down plans.

Only licensed issuers can call their tokens… pic.twitter.com/c5je2ZFzAF

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) September 3, 2026

With the public consultation period ending on 16 October 2026, final commercial launching dates, fee schedules, and projected custody volumes remain dependent on regulatory green lights.

data.title: Hunter Biden Finally Addresses His Laptop Controversy, Saying It Was A Weapon Against Trump
data.description:
Hunter Biden has turned one of the most politically charged controversies surrounding his family into a cryptocurrency aimed at the Trump family’s crypto ventures. But while Biden says his $LAPTOP memecoin was designed to mock what he considers exploitative political tokens, the project’s reported launch and liquidity collapse have raised questions of their own.

In a series of posts on X on Wednesday, Biden defended the token, insisting it was “not a rug pull.” He shared blockchain data showing that 300 million tokens held in wallets associated with the founders had not moved since launch, while pointing to two unnamed market-making firms as the biggest beneficiaries of the project’s trading activity.

2/ Here's why I did this. Trump's coin was max extraction, and I wanted to troll every grift like it. So we were transparent, committed the team to a lock up and published a MiCA disclosure. And I hoped it could help some charities I care about too.

— Hunter Biden (@HunterBiden) October 7, 2026

The token’s name comes from the laptop computer whose existence and contents became a major political flashpoint ahead of the 2020 US presidential election, when Donald Trump was running against Biden’s father, Joe Biden. Years later, the controversy has acquired a crypto afterlife — this time as part of a direct jab at the Trump family’s digital-asset ventures.

A Political Grudge Becomes a Memecoin

Biden said the motivation behind $LAPTOP was to parody what he described as the extractive nature of Trump-associated crypto projects. In his own words, “Trump’s coin was max extraction, and I wanted to troll every grift like it.”

BREAKING: HUNTER BIDEN FINALLY ADDRESSES THE $LAPTOP MEMECOIN CONTROVERSY 🫨 “Yeah man, it’s the anti Trump meme token.” “Here’s the deal, I believe in crypto, I believe in it. They took everything, like they do with everything and they turned what is good into sh**.” “It’s a total grift, and I’m here to prove that it doesn’t have to be that way.”

— One Night with Steiny (@onenightsteiny) September 10, 2026

He said the team sought to distinguish the project through transparency measures, including a token lockup and a disclosure document, while also hoping to direct 5% of the tokens toward charities he supports. According to Biden, founder-associated tokens would remain locked for six months after launch, and the team would continue burning unclaimed airdrop tokens.

But the project was also personal. Biden acknowledged that he was motivated to continue it “just to piss off Don and Eric,” referring to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, as well as key opinion leaders who had called the token a scam after the team refused to pay them for promotion.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 President Trump invites top 185 $TRUMP holders to memecoin dinner. Here we go again. https://t.co/jiCaHVv5ec

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) October 3, 2026

The comments underline how $LAPTOP was positioned as more than a speculative asset. It was also a political provocation, using a controversy that has long been associated with the Biden family to challenge the Trump family’s growing presence in crypto.

That framing, however, does not resolve the question of whether the token’s launch gave ordinary buyers a fair opportunity to trade. For that, the most consequential details lie in the project’s reported liquidity arrangements.

Market Makers Became the Focus After the Price Collapse

Biden acknowledged that $LAPTOP’s price chart “looked like every celebrity rug ever” after its September 9 launch. He attributed much of the fallout to two professional trading firms hired by the project, which he said withdrew liquidity or generated trading profits around the token’s peak.

According to figures shared by Biden, one market maker made approximately $686,000 from liquidity positions on decentralized exchanges, while the other reportedly earned about $2.18 million more than it spent through trading.

LATEST: 🚨 Hunter Biden's LAPTOP memecoin team says its market maker deployed just $5,200 of its $500,000 budget at launch and then pulled its liquidity 84 seconds after the price peaked. https://t.co/9lO4Sr2YWw

— CoinMarketCap (@CoinMarketCap) October 8, 2026

A separate launch report prepared by Delaware-based intelligence consultancy Groom Lake and published on the token’s website described how quickly liquidity available to sellers disappeared. The report said one market maker withdrew its funds 84 seconds after the price peaked, causing the cash available to people trying to sell near the prevailing price to fall from $16,157 to zero.

The report also alleged that the firm received $500,000 before launch but deployed only about $5,200 into the initial liquidity pool. It compared the launch with 668 other token launches and said it found no comparable imbalance. These figures come from the project’s own disclosures and the Groom Lake report, rather than an independent regulatory finding.

$LAPTOP soared within minutes of launch before collapsing almost 99%, becoming one of the wildest political memecoin debuts of the year. The crash followed an extreme launch rally fueled by speculation, low initial liquidity, and intense social media interest around the token’s debut.

— Morkie (@_morkie) September 9, 2026

The distinction matters. A sharp price collapse and a sudden liquidity withdrawal can leave buyers struggling to exit their positions, but those facts alone do not establish that the founders deliberately defrauded investors. Biden’s claim that founder-associated tokens remained untouched addresses one part of the controversy, but it does not by itself settle every question about the launch’s market structure or the experience of traders.

The Trump Family’s Crypto Ventures Return to the Spotlight

The dispute arrives as politically connected memecoins continue to draw scrutiny. Biden has previously criticized World Liberty Financial, the crypto venture backed by the Trump family, calling it “corruption at a scale we’ve never seen” in August.

Trump’s Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin has also faced criticism over its structure and the losses suffered by investors. Public Citizen, a nonprofit consumer advocacy organization, estimated that investors in the token had lost $3.2 billion since its 2025 launch.

LATEST: ⚡️ World Liberty Financial co-founder Zak Folkman says the company plans to bring USD1 payments to "some of the largest Web2 businesses that are in the marketplace." https://t.co/BA5koYC9aw

— CoinMarketCap (@CoinMarketCap) October 8, 2026

The Trump family’s crypto ventures are set to receive further attention on November 22, when President Donald Trump is scheduled to attend a dinner at his Washington, DC, golf club with the top 185 holders of the $TRUMP token, according to an announcement from the group behind the project. Three additional speakers are expected, though their identities were not disclosed in the supplied report.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 President Trump invites top 185 $TRUMP holders to memecoin dinner. Here we go again. https://t.co/jiCaHVv5ec

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) October 3, 2026

Biden’s $LAPTOP project has therefore become part of a wider argument over the role of political figures in speculative crypto markets. His stated intention was to mock what he sees as profiteering through political branding, but the controversy around liquidity and trading has ensured that the token is being judged on its market mechanics as well as its message.

The irony is difficult to miss: a memecoin inspired by a laptop that became a symbol of political conflict is now being used to challenge the Trump family’s crypto ventures. Whether $LAPTOP succeeds as satire is a matter of interpretation. Whether its launch provided a fair trading environment is a separate question — one that requires evidence beyond the founders’ stated intentions.

data.title: TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026: Wall Street Moves Onchain as Crypto's Biggest Week Returns to Marina Bay Sands
data.description:
By Zoey Aemika Ng, Coinlive | Singapore, 8 October 2026

SINGAPORE – TOKEN2049 Singapore returned to Marina Bay Sands on 7–8 October, filling all five floors of the venue with an estimated 25,000 attendees from more than 160 countries, six parallel stages and roughly 500 exhibitors. Organisers said the event had sold out ahead of opening, with over 1,000 side events running across the wider TOKEN2049 Week.

Coinlive attended as media. If the 2025 edition was about the rise of stablecoins and treasury strategies, this year's conversation was noticeably more operational. Across both days, the talk was less about whether traditional finance would enter crypto and more about the plumbing required to make it work: tokenised assets, round-the-clock markets, stablecoin payments and AI agents that move money.

Day One: AI Agents, Privacy and Prediction Markets

The opening day belonged to crypto-native builders. Balaji Srinivasan opened the main stage with a keynote on the open source network state, and Polymarket founder Shayne Coplan used his fireside to reveal that Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, is one of the prediction market's largest shareholders and is exploring onchain equities in dialogue with regulators.

Arthur Hayes of Maelstrom delivered a keynote titled "FLOP Bigger Than Bitcoin", arguing that AI agents will soon number in the millions or billions yet have no native currency, and introducing his new project, FLOP, as an answer. Not everyone on stage agreed that agents are crypto's next big user. Dragonfly's Haseeb Qureshi opened his talk by admitting he was wrong a year ago: agents largely adopted cards rather than crypto payments. His revised thesis is that humans, not agents, are the ones who need crypto, and that agents may become a safety layer that catches phishing and wrong-address mistakes before funds move.

Privacy also had a prominent moment. On a Zcash-themed main stage session, Tyler Winklevoss framed privacy as a human right, while his brother Cameron drew a line between bitcoin as decentralised and public, and Zcash as decentralised and private.

In the afternoon, Eric Trump and World Liberty Financial CEO Zach Witkoff took the stage for "The Future of Finance, Built in America". Trump said the family hospitality business, which employs tens of thousands of people, is looking at paying salaries in stablecoins, and pointed out that conventional paychecks can take 24 to 36 hours to clear. He also said World Liberty plans to tokenise real estate developments with its USD1 stablecoin as the settlement layer.

Elsewhere, Bitmine chairman Tom Lee said the firm will not accumulate ETH beyond 5% of supply, while Aave's Stani Kulechov argued on an institutional DeFi panel that DeFi's lasting advantage is a lower cost structure than traditional finance can match. Hyperliquid Labs CEO Jeff Yan also took the main stage to discuss rebuilding finance from first principles. TOKEN2049's organisers used the first day to announce their US debut: a New York edition in 2027.

Day Two: The Institutions Arrive

If day one asked what crypto will build, day two asked how traditional finance will plug in. BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Morgan Stanley, Nasdaq, ICE and PayPal were all represented in sessions on tokenisation, stablecoins and real-world assets.

Adena Friedman, Nasdaq's chair and CEO, told the main stage that markets are moving toward 24-hour trading, which forces risk management, collateral and the movement of capital to happen in real time. Speaking to CNBC at the event, she said tokenising collateral assets and money could free tens of billions of dollars currently tied up across the financial system.

Jenny Johnson, CEO of Franklin Templeton, joined Binance co-CEO Richard Teng and Canton Network CEO Yuval Rooz on a tokenised markets panel. She said legislation would add certainty but the industry should not wait for the CLARITY Act, since the SEC and CFTC are already providing clarity under existing authority, and criticised rival tokenised funds as mere "digital twins" of traditional products rather than using blockchain as the primary record of ownership.

The day's biggest corporate announcement came from Coinbase, which said its integration of derivatives exchange Deribit is complete, creating Coinbase Global Exchange. Eligible US institutions will be able to access Deribit's products through Coinbase Prime, with options access to follow in the coming weeks.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson pitched Midnight, the network's privacy-focused partner chain, while TRON's Justin Sun predicted that crypto and AI agents could become a major application layer within five years. A regulation panel with SUI Group's Brian Quintenz, Hyperliquid Policy Center's Jake Chervinsky and Kraken's Arjun Sethi focused on cross-border implementation rather than whether crypto should be regulated at all.

An invitation-only TOKEN2049 Institutional track, held for the first time, gathered senior finance and digital asset leaders behind closed doors.

Beyond the Stages

The show floor and surrounding venues ran at full tilt. Formula 1 stars drew crowds, with Lando Norris appearing with OKX on day one and Max Verstappen and Jenson Button featuring on day two, coinciding with Singapore Grand Prix week. The NEXUS startup competition and the Origins hackathon presented their finalists, and the week closes with the official AFTER 2049 party on the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark on 9 October.

Why It Matters

The mood in Singapore reflected an industry still absorbing setbacks, including the recent exchange hacks that dominated hallway conversations and the stalled progress of US market structure legislation, while institutional participation and stablecoin use continue to grow. Tokenised real-world assets have passed US$38 billion, according to RWA.xyz, a small number next to traditional markets but a clear direction of travel. As one theme ran through both days: markets that never close demand infrastructure that never pauses.

Organisers confirmed the 2027 calendar: Dubai on 21–22 April, New York on 16–17 June, and Singapore on 6–7 October.

Coinlive was an attending media partner at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026. Statements attributed to speakers were made on stage or in public remarks at the event. This article is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice.

data.title: Is Webull Really An American Brokerage? US Congress Questions China Control Behind Its 863-Person Workforce
data.description:
A US congressional investigation has raised national security concerns over online brokerage platform Webull, alleging that its ownership, workforce and technology infrastructure have deep ties to China that could expose American investors and their financial data to potential risks.

The bipartisan House Select Committee on China released its findings on 7 October 2026, arguing that Webull’s public image as an American company does not fully reflect its underlying corporate structure and operations.

The report has also raised wider questions about how foreign-linked technology and data systems are used across the financial services industry, including cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset platforms.

A House select committee accused online brokerage Webull of misrepresenting its China-based workforce and technology operations, claiming the connections expose U.S. investor data to Chinese security risks.
Link in thread. pic.twitter.com/WyLGUvV1ut

— The Epoch Times - China Insider (@EpochTimesChina) October 8, 2026

Webull’s China Operations Raise Questions About Investor Data Security

The committee identified six main areas of concern: data management, the location and oversight of key employees, China-linked corporate governance, regulatory controls, government funding received by a Chinese subsidiary, and clearing and custody arrangements.

According to the report, Webull’s software development, data pipelines and core engineering operations depend on systems connected to mainland China, where laws can require companies to co-operate with government authorities, including through the transfer of information.

The committee argued that these connections create potential legal and surveillance risks for US investors.

$BULL bulls, if you want to read the full report on the WeBull findings, you can access it here. The question remains...why the hell would you take the risk? Because they have better charts?https://t.co/cg4djsag5N

— AlaskanInvestor (@FrostyFinances) October 8, 2026

It also said its concerns had increased since October 2025, when Webull began holding customer cash directly, creating what the report described as a “structural exposure of billions of dollars in American capital”.

However, the investigation did not establish that Chinese authorities had accessed US customers’ brokerage accounts or taken control of their assets.

How Deep Do Webull’s Ties To China Go?

Webull’s corporate structure and workforce were central to the investigation.

The company is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and traces its origins to Chinese firm Hunan Fumi Information Technology Co., Ltd.

Founder and chief executive Anquan Wang launched the platform in 2016 after previously holding management positions at Alibaba and Xiaomi.

Although Webull is headquartered in St Petersburg, Florida, its mainland China subsidiary, Hunan Weibu Information Technology, employed 863 people at the end of 2025, accounting for approximately 62% of its total workforce, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

The committee says Hunan Weibu employs 863 people, 62% of Webull's global workforce, and puts customer assets at $24.6bn. Chair John Moolenaar: "Webull's China-based operations put American investors and their data at risk."

— AskTraders (@Asktraders1) October 7, 2026

The committee also questioned the company’s disclosures about its Chinese operations, alleging that information provided to investigators did not adequately account for its mainland China workforce.

Wang held a 16.4% equity stake in Webull but controlled 79.2% of its voting power as of 31 March 2026, giving him substantially greater voting influence than his ownership percentage alone would suggest.

The China link is in Webull's own filings.

Founder Anquan Wang holds 79.0% of the votes with 16.2% of the shares (F-3, Sep 1).

A Hunan unit is building an R&D center in Changsha, due by end-2026 (H1 report, Sep 11).

US inquiries over China ties were already a listed risk.

— Pulkit Arora (@impulkit86) October 7, 2026

The company reports 28.2 million registered users and operates across 18 countries, competing with platforms including Robinhood, Charles Schwab and E-Trade.

The committee cited differing figures for customer assets, including $24.6 billion and $28.5 billion, in its reporting on the company.

Committee chairman John Moolenaar, a Republican representative from Michigan, said Webull’s “China-based operations put American investors and their data at risk”.

Moolenaar said,

“Using technology providers in mainland China and an opaque China-linked ownership structure, Webull exposes its data to our foremost adversary.”

He warned that investors should consider the findings when choosing financial service providers.

Webull Rejects The Allegations And Defends Its Data Controls

Webull disputed the investigation’s conclusions, accusing the committee of publishing inaccurate claims without first seeking clarification from the company.

A company spokesperson said,

“It is deeply disappointing that the Select Committee published a report containing significant inaccuracies and unsupported conclusions without ever seeking clarification from Webull.”

Webull maintains that its US business operates from its global headquarters in St Petersburg and an office in New York City.

It also said its mainland China operations are restricted to research and development and technical support.

In its regulatory filing, the company stated that US customers’ personally identifiable information is stored on servers in the United States.

𝐖𝐄𝐁𝐔𝐋𝐋 𝐓𝐎𝐋𝐃 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐆𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒 𝐈𝐓 𝐇𝐀𝐒 𝐍𝐎 𝐄𝐌𝐏𝐋𝐎𝐘𝐄𝐄𝐒 𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐇𝐈𝐍𝐀

The House Select Committee on China released findings Wednesday saying the trading app Webull, which markets itself as an American company, keeps “𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬” 𝐭𝐨… pic.twitter.com/P0GgegVNBB

— M.A. Rothman (@MichaelARothman) October 8, 2026

Access by employees outside the country requires permission and oversight from US personnel, according to the filing.

The spokesperson added that “U.S. customer data is stored in the U.S. and access to sensitive customer data is controlled by the U.S.”

The company said it remained willing to answer questions from regulators, including the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority.

The committee has proposed stronger oversight of broker-dealers with foreign links and additional safeguards for brokerage data involving foreign adversaries.

It also raised the possibility of bringing foreign-controlled broker-dealers under the jurisdiction of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS).

Webull Shares Fall As Investors Weigh The Investigation

The report triggered a sharp decline in Webull’s share price as investors assessed the potential implications of the allegations.

Webull Corp (BULL) fell as much as 32% in pre-market trading before closing down 19.09% at $5.89 on Wednesday, 7 October.

📉 $BULL $5.92 printed $4.93 premarket (-32%), then trimmed the loss; regular-session range 5.51–6.02.

🎯 The 52-week low at $4.50 is the next reference if selling resumes.

👀 Watch Webull's response and any regulator follow-up.#Webull#Stocks#China#Markets

— Noctiz.eth (@NoctizXIII) October 7, 2026

The shares dropped a further 3% on Thursday, closing at approximately $5.70.

The investigation does not establish that customer funds or personal information have been compromised.

However, the scrutiny could expose the company to greater regulatory pressure as US lawmakers examine the risks associated with foreign-linked financial infrastructure.

Could The Same Concerns Extend To Crypto Exchanges And Digital Wallets?

The investigation raises questions that extend beyond traditional stockbroking.

Cryptocurrency exchanges, digital asset custodians and wallet providers also depend on technology infrastructure, engineering teams and data management systems that may operate across multiple jurisdictions.

For these platforms, the central issue is not simply where a company is headquartered, but who controls its underlying systems, where sensitive information is stored and who can access it.

Foreign ownership, cross-border data flows and reliance on overseas technical teams could become areas of concern if regulators believe they create national security or investor protection risks.

The Webull case does not establish that cryptocurrency platforms face the same risks or that foreign-linked companies have improperly accessed customer information.

Instead, it illustrates how corporate ownership, technology dependencies and control over financial data can attract greater scrutiny when lawmakers view them as potential national security vulnerabilities.

As US authorities consider stronger oversight of foreign-linked financial firms, digital asset businesses could face similar questions about the security and control of the infrastructure supporting customers’ funds and information.

data.title: US Government Moves More Than $1.7B In Seized Bitcoin As Mystery Transfers Fuel Questions
data.description:
The US government has secretly moved billions of dollars’ worth of Bitcoin through a series of recent transactions, including a $770 million transfer to Coinbase Prime and a separate $1.01 billion movement of Bitcoin seized in connection with the Bitfinex hack.

US government moves 9,261 $$BTC to Coinbase Prime, including 2,456 $$BTC potentially from new seizures "US government moves $770 million in Bitcoin to Coinbase Prime. Is Bitcoin facing a massive sell-off? Well, I mean, it's down a little bit. Is it because the US government is dumping $770 million in Bitcoin? Absolutely not." "This is from Galaxy Research, who tracks these wallets. There's also actually another report of another $100 million that was tracked by Arkham that's completely separate from this, by the way." "Galaxy Research says government-linked wallets transferred 9,261 Bitcoin worth approximately $770 million to Coinbase Prime Tuesday and Wednesday. So they can link this actually to where this Bitcoin came from - roughly half to the Bitfinex hackers and another portion to known Binance seizures, right? That was obviously back in the Binance case." "The Bitfinex Bitcoin are very, very interesting because those probably should belong to Bitfinex. That's a story for another day. So an additional 2,456 of the Bitcoin came from previously unidentified holdings and may represent new law enforcement seizures that we have not yet heard about."

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) October 8, 2026

The transfers have reignited questions about how Washington is managing its massive crypto holdings, but there is no confirmed evidence that the government has sold the assets.

According to Galaxy Research, government-linked wallets transferred 9,261 Bitcoin (BTC) worth approximately $770 million to Coinbase Prime over Oct. 6 and 7. A separate transaction tracked by Arkham showed 12,267 BTC, valued at roughly $1.01 billion, moving from a wallet linked to the Bitfinex hack seizure to a new, unlabeled address.

The movements involve different reported transactions and destinations, and on-chain data alone cannot establish whether the transfers involved separate underlying holdings or were part of a broader sequence of wallet movements. What they do reveal is the scale and complexity of the government’s ongoing management of seized digital assets.

$770M Reaches Coinbase Prime as 2,456 BTC Raises New Questions

The Coinbase Prime transfers involved Bitcoin recovered from previous crypto-related cases. Galaxy Research said nearly half of the 9,261 BTC was linked to the Bitfinex hack, while another portion came from known Binance-related seizures.

While Heather Morgan is poised to start a prison sentence in the @bitfinex hack, alter ego “Razzlekhan” has dropped a new rap video. @jesseahamilton reports on the latest from @HeatherReyhan https://t.co/kzlfUdeLKp

— CoinDesk (@CoinDesk) January 10, 2025

The transfers arrived in two batches, according to the figures cited in the supplied reporting. Approximately 834 BTC moved on Oct. 6, followed by 8,428 BTC on Oct. 7, bringing the total to 9,261 BTC. Galaxy also highlighted an additional 2,456 BTC originating from wallets that had not previously been identified as government-linked.

Second trigger: the US government moved a large amount of seized Bitcoin. On October 8, 12,267 BTC (about $1.01B) left a wallet holding funds seized in the 2016 Bitfinex hack. It went to new, unlabeled addresses. A day earlier, about 3,200 BTC ($264M) and $119M in USDT went to Coinbase Prime deposit addresses. Traders are reading this as a sign the government may sell. But There is no sign of a sale yet.

— Bull Theory (@BullTheoryio) October 8, 2026

Those coins were sent to a government seizure address on Coinbase Prime, leading Galaxy to suggest they may represent additional law enforcement seizures. However, the origin of the funds has not been independently confirmed, and no official announcement has established that the Bitcoin came from a newly concluded enforcement action.

Coinbase Prime has served as a custody provider for digital assets handled by the US Marshals Service since 2024. Because the platform offers institutional custody as well as trading and settlement services, a transfer to Coinbase Prime does not, by itself, prove that the government intends to sell the Bitcoin.

A separate transaction involving Bitcoin seized from the 2016 Bitfinex hack added another layer of uncertainty. Arkham data showed a government-linked wallet transferring 12,267 BTC, worth approximately $1.01 billion, to a new, unlabeled address on Oct. 8. A tiny amount of 0.0012 BTC was sent to a second address.

Chính phủ Mỹ chuyển khoảng 470 triệu USD crypto tới Coinbase Prime Theo Arkham, các ví gắn nhãn chính phủ Mỹ đã chuyển khoảng 470 triệu USD gồm BTC, WBTC và USDT tới các địa chỉ nạp được gắn nhãn có khả năng thuộc Coinbase Prime. Phần lớn tài sản liên quan các vụ thu giữ từ hacker Bitfinex (2016) và từ FTX/Alameda. Chuyển lên Coinbase Prime chưa đồng nghĩa với bán. Từ năm 2024, Coinbase Prime là nơi US Marshals Service lưu ký tài sản số bị tịch thu, nên đây có thể chỉ là bước gom tài sản trước khi có quyết định giữ, hoàn trả hoặc thanh lý. Một số tracker cùng ngày còn ghi nhận các dòng chuyển liên quan khác, đẩy tổng quan sát được lên khoảng 560 triệu USD nếu cộng cả USDT và BNB. Con số 470 triệu USD là mốc Arkham nêu trực tiếp. Chú ý : Chỉ là thông tin tham khảo , không phải lời khuyên đầu tư.

— KEN NC (@giahan220522) October 8, 2026

The funds are linked to the roughly 94,000 BTC seized in 2022 from Ilya Lichtenstein, who orchestrated the Bitfinex hack, and his wife, Heather Morgan. The original 2016 attack saw 119,754 BTC stolen from the exchange, making the recovered assets one of the most significant pools of Bitcoin ever brought under US government control.

Unlike the Coinbase Prime transfers, the $1.01 billion movement did not send the bulk of the Bitcoin directly to a known exchange address. Arkham subsequently marked the transaction outputs as spent, indicating that the coins had moved again, but those movements do not establish that the Bitcoin was sold.

The two sets of transfers have nevertheless drawn attention because they involve large sums, different wallet destinations and assets tied to high-profile crypto enforcement cases. Without further information from authorities, it remains unclear whether the activity reflects routine custody changes, internal wallet restructuring or other operational steps.

Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Complicates Sale Speculation

The transfers have also revived questions about whether the US government could liquidate some of its seized Bitcoin. Similar wallet movements have triggered speculation in the past, but the current policy framework points toward retaining forfeited Bitcoin rather than routinely selling it.

In March 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve. The order directs that Bitcoin finally forfeited through criminal or civil proceedings and deposited into the reserve should not be sold, subject to specified legal and operational exceptions.

For now, the recent transfers offer no definitive evidence of a government Bitcoin sell-off. Instead, they highlight the challenges of tracking a large, distributed pool of seized assets using public blockchain data, where transactions are visible but their purpose is not always clear. Until federal authorities explain the movements, the central question remains how Washington is organizing and managing its Bitcoin holdings as the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve takes shape.
